About Us
Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.
The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.
Role Summary
The Infotainment Platform team at Rivian Volkswagen Technologies is looking for a skilled Software Engineer to join our Automotive Software team. We are developing the next generation, Android-based in-vehicle experience that will be deployed across all future electric vehicles in the Rivian and Volkswagen Group portfolios. You will work on the architecture, integration, and optimization of both display and input subsystems for our next-generation infotainment platforms. In this role, you will own the end-to-end pipeline from the low-level hardware drivers (touch controllers, display panels, physical buttons) up through the OS frameworks (Linux, QNX, Android Automotive) to ensure a seamless, highly responsive, and visually flawless user experience.
Join us in driving the future of automotive infotainment!
Responsibilities
Display & Graphics Pipeline: Develop, integrate, and maintain display drivers and compositor frameworks (e.g., DRM/KMS, SurfaceFlinger, Wayland, OpenWFD) for complex, multi-display automotive topologies.
Touch & Input Subsystems: Develop and integrate drivers and middleware for touch panels (capacitive, resistive) and physical infotainment buttons (e.g., hard keys, rotary dials, steering wheel controls). Optimize input processing, gesture recognition, multi-touch coordination, and noise filtering within the OS input frameworks (e.g., Android InputFlinger, Linux evdev).
Performance Optimization: Tune the complete glass-to-glass pipeline. Optimize frame rates, visual quality (color accuracy, white point tuning), and touch/button latency to ensure a fluid, highly responsive user experience.
Hardware Bring-Up & Integration: Partner closely with hardware vendors and SoC partners to bring up new display panels (LCD, OLED) and input interfaces via standard buses (MIPI DSI, I2C, SPI) and SerDes links.
System-Level Debugging: Investigate and resolve complex display and input issues (e.g., screen freezes, visual artifacts, touch ghosting, missed button presses, dropped frames) using software profilers, gdb, JTAG, and logic analyzers.
Feature Development: Implement advanced system features such as dynamic backlight control, power sequencing, resolution switching, fault monitoring, and multi-display synchronization.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with Hardware engineers, UI/UX designers, and System teams to define requirements, document software architectures, and ensure compliance with automotive safety and EMC requirements.
Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications:
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
3+ years of proven experience in embedded software development or platform engineering, specifically focusing on display panels, touch screens, and hardware input technologies.
Strong proficiency in C/C++ programming.
Deep understanding of embedded operating systems such as Linux, QNX, or Android Automotive OS.
Solid grasp of display and input frameworks (e.g., Linux DRM/KMS, Android SurfaceFlinger/InputManager).
Experience with hardware peripherals and interfaces (I2C, SPI, UART, MIPI DSI).
Excellent problem-solving, system-level debugging, and teamwork skills.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience bringing up automotive infotainment platforms on major SoCs (e.g., Qualcomm Snapdragon, NXP).
Familiarity with graphics libraries and hardware compositors (OpenGL ES, Vulkan, HWC).
Experience with automotive communication protocols (CAN, Automotive Ethernet).
Familiarity with display virtualization (VirtIO-GPU) and hypervisor environments (e.g., QNX, Gunyah).
Proficiency with performance profiling tools like Systrace, Perfetto, and vendor-specific GPU profilers.

Payments are discretionary and not guaranteed; actual amounts depend on company results and the terms of the plan in effect, and require active employment at the time of payout. Description
Training and running large AI models takes enormous amounts of expensive accelerated compute, and most of it sits idle. Across the industry, a large share of GPU capacity is paid for but never does useful work because jobs cannot find it, cannot share it, or cannot see it and use it efficiently. We build the services that closes that gap.
We are looking for a Software Development Engineer to help build the systems that put idle or inefficiently used GPUs to work. You will design and build distributed backend services that let organizations pool capacity across many clusters and accounts, route it to the workloads that need it most, and see exactly how it is being used. This is deep systems work at the intersection of large-scale distributed systems, container orchestration, and cloud infrastructure, and it directly changes how much value customers get from every GPU they pay for.
You will own services end to end, from design through launch and operation in production, and your work will ship to some of the largest AI compute customers in the world.
Key job responsibilities
Design, build, and operate distributed backend services that manage and share accelerated compute across multiple clusters and accounts.
Build scheduling and capacity-sharing capabilities that move compute to the highest-priority workloads and reclaim it when priorities change.
Build zero-touch usage and guidance systems that collect, aggregate, and report how compute is consumed, at scale and in near real time.
Own your services in production: define operational metrics, respond to issues, and continuously improve reliability, latency, and cost.
Write clear design documents, participate in design and code reviews, and raise the engineering bar for the team.
Collaborate with product, design, and partner engineering teams to turn customer problems into shipped features.
Mentor other engineers and contribute to a culture of ownership, quality, and customer focus.
A day in the life
Most days start with a short team stand-up, then it is mostly building. You might design a service that lets one cluster borrow idle capacity from another, then write it up for a design review where the team pokes holes in it before any code is written. Hard problems get their own deep-dive whiteboard session. Other days lean toward operations, chasing down why a workload did not get the capacity it should have. You will not be handed fully specified tasks; you will have the independence to help decide what to build, then build it.
About The Team
We help customers get the most out of the accelerated compute they pay for. Our mission is simple to say and hard to do: make sure every accelerator a customer pays for is doing useful work, and make that easy to see and control. Cost reduction is one important part of that, but the bigger idea is the engine that delivers compute to the workloads that need it most, in as little time as possible.
Our customers run some of the largest AI training and inference workloads in the world, and they feel the impact of our work directly in how much they can do with their infrastructure. We care about depth, we own our work end to end, and we build in the open where we can.

Candidate must effectively and cooperatively work as a team member of a multi-discipline, integrated project team. The I&C engineer/tech will routinely perform walkdowns in the existing plant facilities in order to generate design documents and provide field support to craft personnel.

Responsibilities
The Signal & Measurement team at TikTok Ads owns the full stack of advertising effectiveness — from signal collection and identity resolution to attribution modeling and causal measurement. We build the systems and models that help advertisers worldwide understand and maximize the true business value of their ad spend on TikTok.
Our work sits at the intersection of large-scale machine learning and causal inference, applied at massive scale to answer the hardest question in advertising: "Did this ad actually work?" The team's scope covers four pillars: signal, attribution, identity, and measurement. These outputs directly power downstream ads ranking and delivery models, closing the loop from measurement back to optimization. As a new grad on the team, you will be paired with an experienced mentor, own real projects from day one, and grow across both machine learning and large-scale systems.
We are looking for talented individuals to join our team. As a graduate, you will get opportunities to pursue bold ideas, tackle complex challenges, and unlock limitless growth.

Responsibilities:
Build and improve machine learning models for signal quality — anomaly detection, signal recovery, denoising, and correction — to ensure the reliability of advertiser conversion data at scale.
Contribute to cross-platform identity resolution: improve the precision and coverage of our Identity Graph through probabilistic matching models and graph algorithms.

Building Devin is just the first step—our hardest challenges still lie ahead. If you’re excited to solve some of the world’s biggest problems and build AI that can reason on real-world tasks, apply to join us.
Role Mission
Mid-training sits at the seam between pre-training and post-training and is one of the highest-leverage points in the entire model pipeline. This is where raw base model capability is sharpened into something that can reason deeply, generalize reliably, and serve as the foundation that post-training builds on.
You will own the late-stage training decisions that determine what our models are fundamentally capable of: data mix and quality uplift, annealing schedules, context length extension, capability injection across coding, math, and reasoning, and the synthetic data strategies that make all of it scale. This role does cross-cutting work across what is classically considered both pre-training and post-training. We don't distinguish between research and engineering; we expect both.
What You'll Accomplish
Data Mix and Quality Uplift: Design and iterate on high-quality data mixtures for late-stage and annealing training runs. Develop principled methods for sourcing, filtering, and weighting data to sharpen model capabilities without degrading general performance.
Capability Injection: Drive targeted improvements in coding, mathematics, and long-horizon reasoning through curated data strategies and training interventions. Translate research insights into measurable capability gains on our agents.
Synthetic Data Research: Develop and evaluate synthetic data pipelines that generate training signal at scale. Understand the limits and failure modes of synthetic approaches and build methods that hold up in production training runs.
Annealing and Schedule Design: Research and optimize multi-stage learning rate schedules, warmup strategies, and compute allocation across training phases. Understand how schedule choices interact with data distribution and model behavior.
Context Length Extension: Research and implement methods for extending effective context length without degrading short-context performance. This includes positional encoding strategies, data construction, and targeted evaluation.
Evaluation and Iteration: Build evals that distinguish real capability improvements from benchmark overfitting. Close the loop between training decisions and what actually matters for Devin and our other systems in deployment.
Scaling and Methodology: Measure how mid-training interventions scale with compute and data. Develop new approaches when existing methods hit ceilings; we expect both rigorous empiricism and original thinking.
Exceptional Candidates Have Demonstrated
Deep familiarity with the LLM training pipeline end to end: pre-training data, optimization, architecture, and how mid-training and post-training interact
Hands-on experience with continual pre-training, annealing, or late-stage data mixing for large models
Strong intuition for data quality: what makes a dataset useful for training, how to filter and curate at scale, and how data mix choices compound across evals
Experience developing or evaluating synthetic data pipelines for capability improvement
Proficiency in Python and deep learning frameworks (PyTorch); comfortable debugging distributed training at scale
Strong fundamentals in optimization, statistics, and ML theory; able to distinguish real effects from noise, instability, and overfitting
A track record of original contributions: publications, open-source impact, or internal results that moved a capability frontier
Comfort operating in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where the problem definition is as important as the solution
We care more about demonstrated capability than credentials. A PhD is one signal among many.
Resources & Environment
Small, highly selective team where research and product move together; prototypes reach real deployment quickly
Compute is not a constraint: large allocations with training jobs routinely running across thousands of GPUs from day one
The environment rewards speed, autonomy, and technical depth with minimal process overhead; this is one of the most competitive and fast-moving problems in AI

What is Spade?
Financial institutions process billions of transactions every day across cards, ACH, wires, and third party aggregators. But most of that data is difficult to use. Descriptions are inconsistent, merchant names don’t match, and categories vary by payment type.
Spade is a data and AI platform that turns messy transaction strings into structured, verified records — and gives teams the tools to act on it across authorization, attribution, analytics, and AI initiatives. Spade leads the market in terms of merchant coverage, matching accuracy, geolocation data, and speed of transaction enrichment. Customers such as, FIS, Bilt, Mercury, Stripe, alongside many other leaders in fintech and financial services, trust Spade's data to enable personalized rewards programs, accurate applied spending rules, precise analytics requests, and innovative AI-powered features.
Spade is a fast growing, Series B company backed by industry experts and top tier investors (including Oak HC/FT, a16z, Flourish Ventures, Y-Combinator, and Gradient Ventures). We’re a lean and execution-oriented hybrid team, passionate about building exceptional products for our growing customer base. We care deeply about diversity of background, experience, and opinion. We value empathy, curiosity, and passion, and strive to create an environment where individuals have autonomy and the ability to take ownership over their work.
The Opportunity
As a Full Stack Engineer at Spade, you’ll own product experiences end-to-end, working across both the frontend and backend of our enrichment platform. You’ll build customer-facing interfaces in React and TypeScript, as well as the Python/Django APIs, data models, and platform services that power them. This is a high-ownership role on a small team, where your decisions will directly shape the usability, performance, and reliability of products processing billions of transactions.

Collaborate on our technical vision to build a product customers love
Build and maintain customer-facing product experience across React/TypeScript on the frontend and Python/Django on the backend
Develop and maintain low-latency, massively-scalable developer facing APIs and a robust data platform supporting our data science team
Partner with the team to own and improve our engineering best practices and help us scale by keeping our processes effective
Debug production issues across all levels of the stack
Bring a strong collaborative approach to deliver value to customers and internal stakeholders at Spade
What experience, skills, and qualifications are necessary?
Must Have:
4+ years of software engineering experience building and shipping production systems in fast-paced environments
Strong background with Python, Django, React, and Typescript
Experience with API development, SQL, and modern front end frameworks and technologies
Experience building customer-facing systems from scratch, making trade-offs, and executing autonomously in early-stage environments
A product mindset and strong problem solving skills, with the ability to navigate ambiguity and focus on delivering customer value
A collaborative mindset, fostering a culture shared success and continuous improvement
Based in NYC with ability to work out of our Flatiron office at least 2 days/week
Nice to Have:
Experience with Aurora RDS Postgres
Experience with managing cloud infrastructure via tools like AWS CDK
Experience with transaction, merchant, and location data
Familiarity with fintech / data products

Why Join Spade?
Be a cultural founder. As an early employee, you’ll play a meaningful role in defining and building our culture.
Get in on the ground floor. We’re a small but well-funded team – joining now comes with limited risk and unlimited upside.
Build the next generation of financial infrastructure. Our products will power the next wave of innovation in fintech, helping our customers deliver better, more transparent products and services to the consumer.

Competitive Compensation. Data-driven salaries that reward performance and ownership.
Meaningful Equity. Flexibility with early exercise and an extended post-termination options.
Comprehensive Health Benefits. 100% paid medical, mental, dental, and vision premium option plus One Medical membership (for US-based employees).
401(k). Empowering you to invest in your future.
Paid Parental Leave. 12 weeks of full pay for parents welcoming a new child into their home.

Supporting you in and outside of work. Generous work from home stipend, company-paid lunches, Citibike Membership, and more.

The backbone of any technology org is its infrastructure, come join the team giving that skeleton superhuman abilities. The Infrastructure team at Mercury is an enablement lever for the rest of the business, building scaleable, secure and maintainable foundations for the rest of the org to build on top of.
Infrastructure is currently building out more platform features to make it easier for agents and humans to deploy code. This means security by default, observable by default and easy to use and operate. We do all this while not compromising on speed, and ship to prod all day, every day, which is a testament to the strong foundations this team has built.
We are looking for an engineer to join our team to help build out the “platform” even further! We maintain everything from networking to container orchestration, and work with product teams to enable any AWS needs they have. We want someone who is passionate about building maintainable systems, is obsessed with quality and making sure the sharp edges are filed off, and is extremely helpful when diving into problems with our product counterparts.
This is a role for someone who likes going deep, shipping often, and leaving systems better than they found them. Someone who cares about quality without turning quality into bureaucracy. Someone who is just as happy debugging a strange Linux problem as they are helping a product engineer understand why their service behaves differently in production.
Some of the technology you’ll work with
Our infrastructure is built primarily on AWS, including systems like EC2, RDS, OpenSearch, ECS, and EKS. We like to use the right tool for the job and bias towards cloud native open source tooling
We use Terraform extensively to manage infrastructure as code, GitHub and GitHub Actions for version control and delivery, and Prometheus, Grafana, OpenSearch, and OpenTelemetry to understand what is happening in production.
We’re also increasingly building
agentic infrastructure
: systems that let AI agents safely interact with our infrastructure, and frameworks that give both agents and the humans operating them the right guardrails.
You do not need to arrive knowing every tool we use. We care more about strong fundamentals, curiosity, and the ability to go deep.
As we gear up for the next stages of Mercury's growth, you will:
Build our “Infrastructure Platform” to support the growing needs of the Engineering Organization
Focus on building a platform that is AI friendly while still usable for engineers. We want our users to be humans and Agents
Deliver key infrastructure projects, break-down complex initiatives, and define our infrastructure strategy through detailed RFCs and technical specifications
Must haves:
You have 2+ years of experience with AWS
You have a keen interest in cloud native open source technologies, and feel comfortable contributing code upstream to these technologies
Strong knowledge of low-level operating system foundations (linux, file systems, containers, etc)
You have demonstrated ability in technical writing, with at least 2 years of experience creating detailed technical documentation, RFCs, and tech specs that clearly communicate complex ideas
The ideal candidate should:
Be used to operating in regulated environments such as HITRUST or SOC2, ensuring compliance and security
Have 2+ years of experience working in massive terraform environments, with many engineers contributing code in a scalable way
Have 2+ years of experience writing code. We are building an Infrastructure Platform from scratch and there is plenty of code to write to support that
Be extremely willing to learn and dive into hard problems! We have many to solve!
The Infrastructure team sits in an interesting place at Mercury: close enough to production that the details matter, and broad enough that a good abstraction can make hundreds of engineers faster.
There is a lot left to build.
If you like infrastructure that is secure by default, observable by default, pleasant to use, and designed for people who want to ship, we’d love to hear from you.

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.
The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

About The Role
Corporate Security at Ramp owns the security of our internal environment: the device fleet, the identity and access layer, and the AI tools employees use for their work. We are hiring a Systems Engineer to build and operate the controls across these systems.
The role is hands-on, writing code and building agentic loops wherever possible rather than solving problems manually. You will help manage device configuration and patching via configuration-as-code, authentication and authenticator policies in Okta, network and gateway enforcement in Cloudflare, and the controls around our enterprise Claude and OpenAI deployments. These systems overlap heavily in practice, and the work is largely about integrating them and automating what would otherwise be manual administration.

Maintain device configuration baselines as code, including drift detection and hardening standards

Remediate identity posture gaps surfaced by ISPM tooling: stale accounts, orphaned service principals, over-scoped OAuth grants, MFA gaps, and excess privileges
Implement and operate controls for enterprise AI usage, including identity-aware access, logging and retention, DLP where appropriate, and enforcement
Automate across these platforms using their APIs, build reporting on control coverage, and document how the controls you build are operated

Experience with EDR and endpoint vulnerability management (CrowdStrike or similar)

We're building a new kind of software stack: a hardware-agnostic platform that makes every system — from a laptop to a supercomputer — feel like one seamless engine. If you love digging into instruction selection, register allocation, and low-level target-specific optimization and you want that work to matter at the scale of the next era of AI infrastructure, this role is for you.

Design, develop, maintain, and improve our heterogeneous AI compiler.
Design and implement new code generation capabilities based on our novel compiler architecture.
Propose improvements and extensions to our compiler architecture in response to advances in ML model design and hardware.
Apply the latest techniques in parallelization and partitioning to automate kernel generation and exploit highly optimized execution paths.
Use performance data to identify optimization opportunities and drive measurable improvements.
Collaborate with our product team to understand the evolving needs of ML engineers and translate those needs into architectural improvements.

BS degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.
4+ years of experience working with compilers.
Deep knowledge of compiler algorithms and data structures.
Experience with and genuine interest in low-level code generation, object file manipulation, and target-specific optimizations.
4+ years of experience with C/C++.
Strong written and verbal communication skills; ability to write clear and concise technical documentation.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Master's or PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent.
Knowledge of traditional compiler techniques: instruction selection, register allocation, dominance analysis, def-use chains.
Familiarity with calling conventions, APIs, linking, and relocations.
Working knowledge of LLVM.
Experience with loop optimizations, vectorization, unrolling, fusion, and parallelization.
Experience with machine learning workloads and their hardware demands.
Why Join Lemurian Labs
Work on compiler infrastructure that runs AI at scale across every major hardware platform.
Tackle deep, unsolved technical problems alongside a team that prizes craft and rigor.
Be part of building sustainable AI infrastructure that genuinely moves the needle.

About AIUC
AIUC builds standards and insurance for frontier AI. Our mission is to Underwrite superintelligence. We exist because risk, not capability, is becoming the binding constraint on AI being useful. History offers lessons for how to build confidence in new technology; electricity burned down houses until insurers funded Underwriters Laboratories (UL) to certify products against their standards. Today, the UL mark is a trustmark on every light bulb in America. We’re building that for AI.
AIUC-1, our standard for agent security, serves frontier builders like Cursor, Lovable, ElevenLabs, and Harvey. We've raised $55m from Ribbit, First Harmonic and Nat Friedman to audit frontier AI. Our team comes from METR, Anthropic, McKinsey, and OpenAI. Come join us.
The Role
Every AI company that comes to us wants the same thing: proof their agent is safe enough to sell to an enterprise. Getting there means running thousands of evaluations against their live system.
We've now certified the category leaders in every major AI vertical: ElevenLabs (voice), Intercom (customer service), UiPath (workflow automation), Lovable (coding), and more we'll announce soon. No two of those systems look alike: each has its own authentication, its own interface, its own definition of what a failure even looks like. Before we can test any of it, someone has to sit with that customer, understand how their agent actually works, and get it wired into our evaluation system.
We're hiring an
engineer to own that work end to end
. You'll have your own set of customers within your first weeks, paired with a commercial counterpart on each one.
In This Role, You Will
Own the path from signed customer to delivered results - scoping what to test, working through their authentication and interfaces, and getting their agent running in our system
Build the one-off version when a customer doesn't fit the product yet, and make it work anyway
Deliver results directly to the customer and be the person they trust with the technical detail
Make the call on whether a customer meets the AIUC-1 standard
Work across the widest surface of any role here: our Delivery team, our core engineers, sales, the Standards team (shaping what goes into AIUC-1), and your customer's own engineering team
Turn what you learn in the field into the product
That last one is why the role exists. We're building toward a product that runs evaluations end to end without an engineer in the loop. This is a high-agency role: you'll shape what we build next as much as you'll deliver what we've built.
If you're planning to start a company one day, this is a front row seat. You'll work directly with our founders, with founders at the companies we certify, and alongside a team full of ex-founders.
What We're Looking For
The job in practice looks like reading someone's API docs, chasing credentials, building integrations into customers' systems and agents. Then evaluating whether those agents behave, and owning the failure modes the evals surface. The person who thrives here has done this work before. What drives them is trust and safety.
To Be Successful, We Think You Have
3-7 years of experience, likely as an early engineer at a startup where you ended up owning customers, or in an integration, solutions, or forward deployed role selling technical products to technical buyers. (Impact matters more than years.)

Customer obsession: their problem is your problem, and you see it through

Experience founding or co-founding a company
Experience with AI evaluations or red-teaming
Executive presence with senior stakeholders
Our Values
We are in the business of building trust. We take our values seriously and treat them as commitments to each other, held to the same bar as the ones we make to customers.
Strong back: high standards, keep our promises, work hard.
Fast feet: experiment, cut scope, take delight in pace.
Eyes up: wrestle with the mission, and let where AI is heading shape our strategy, our teams and our day-to-day work.
Open heart: say the scary thing, create connection, make room for emotions.
Underwriting superintelligence is our life's work. If you want it to be yours, apply now.

Equity (significant part of total compensation)
Health, dental and vision insurance for you and your dependents
Visa sponsorship and relocation stipend to bring you to SF, if needed

A software engineer who chose infrastructure.

Characterize and debug laser behavior using optical test and measurement equipment, and build the automated test and data collection scripts that make that work repeatable.

Experience contributing embedded software to a product that shipped to customers, or to hardware that reached production or field deployment.
Proficiency in C or C++, and comfort with Python for tooling, test, and analysis.

Working knowledge of Git, and experience with CMake or a comparable build system.

Coursework, research, or industry experience in closed-loop control: designing, simulating, or deploying control algorithms on real systems.
Experience developing firmware for optical transceivers, photonic systems, or other precision analog/mixed-signal hardware.

Engineering autonomy: Here, business decisions are made by business people, and technical decisions are made by technical people.

As a Software Engineer 3 focused on security within Engineering Experience (EngExp), you help drive the team's evolution from DevOps to DevSecOps. You turn raw findings (Wiz, Veracode, pentest reports) into evidence-backed, actionable guidance. Triage and respond to vulnerabilities identified through tools such as Wiz, Veracode, and penetration tests, and help drive them to resolution

You write maintainable code in at least one general-purpose language such as Go, Java, Kotlin, or TypeScript. Scripting alone isn't enough. You have built and maintained a tool, service, or controller that other people rely on, with tests and code review.

Partner with engineers to articulate the actual threat (or lack of one) behind a code or infrastructure finding
Remediate findings directly when you have the context - whether in EngExp's own infrastructure or another team's - and drive remediation through partnership where you don't
Integrate security checks (SAST/DAST) into GitLab CI/CD pipelines so issues are caught at build and merge-request time, not only in point-in-time scans
Contribute to security standards and best practices, and coach teams through adopting them
Help verify AI-proposed fixes and risk assessments against the actual code, config, and runtime context before they're accepted
Technologies We Use
Application security tools: Veracode, Wiz
SAST/DAST tooling embedded in CI/CD
Vulnerability management and ticketing systems (Jira or equivalent)
Cloud environments: AWS, Kubernetes
Infrastructure as Code: Terraform and Kubernetes manifests
CI/CD pipelines and developer platforms (GitLab CI/CD, ArgoCD)
Programming languages: comfortable reading and fixing code in at least one of Python, Go, or the JVM languages (Java, Scala, Kotlin) - CJ's codebases span all of these

What we look for:
3+ years of software or infrastructure engineering experience, with hands-on exposure to application or infrastructure security

About Levelpath
Backed by some of the top venture capital firms in Silicon Valley and founded by third-time founders with two successful exits, Levelpath is building autonomous procurement.
We've built an agentic software factory that accelerates our development by an order of magnitude. Everything we learn about harnessing AI to build software goes into the product, driving faster, more accurate, and safer outcomes for enterprise procurement teams. We build with the aggressive assumption that everything in procurement can be done by AI. Our job is to prove it.
Autonomy only counts when it connects to the systems an enterprise already runs. Nothing makes Levelpath real for a customer faster than the moment their ERP, HRIS, and financial systems start talking to us. That moment is this job.
The role
You will own the connective tissue between Levelpath and the systems our customers already run: ERPs like NetSuite, SAP, and Oracle, plus HRIS, SSO, ticketing, e-signature, and finance tools. Some integrations you build yourself. Others are built by customer teams, and you are the engineer who guides them, unblocks them, and makes sure everything works in production.
This is a customer-facing engineering role in the truest sense. You will be on calls with customer IT and integration teams, whiteboarding data flows, debugging auth handshakes live, and turning ambiguous requirements into working pipelines. When a customer's integration engineer is stuck, you are the person who gets them moving again.
You will build with our agentic software factory, and you will improve it. The factory is optimized for exactly this work: well-specified contracts and a premium on verification. It is not perfect, and when it falls short you fix the cause, contributing tooling back so the next integration ships faster. Agents are the execution capacity here. Your job is to drive them to the outcome: unblock them when they stall, correct them when they drift, and verify what they ship.
You will also be the engineering presence in the US timezone. Our core platform team is distributed internationally, and you help anchor US-hours on-call coverage so customers get a fast, expert response no matter when things break. On-call is a real part of this role, and we invest in the observability, runbooks, and agent tooling that make it sane.
What you will do
Design, build, and ship integrations between Levelpath and enterprise systems (ERP, HRIS, SSO/SCIM, ticketing, e-signature) using TypeScript, NestJS, and PostgreSQL in an agent-driven workflow.
Lead technical calls with customer engineering and IT teams: scoping, architecture reviews, debugging sessions, and go-live support.
Guide customers building against our GraphQL API and MCP surface, from first webhook to production cutover.
Harden integration paths for the realities of enterprise data: schema enforcement, validation, retries, idempotency, and graceful degradation.
Anchor US-hours on-call, triaging production issues and improving the tooling that makes the next incident easier.
Feed what you learn in the field back into the product: better connectors, better docs, better defaults.
What you bring
Solid backend or full-stack fundamentals with several years shipping production software.
Real experience with third-party APIs and integration work: REST and GraphQL, webhooks, OAuth and SAML flows, data mapping, and the patience to read someone else's API docs carefully.
AI-pilled, genuinely. Your instinct is to hand work to agents first, and you want to turn over as much as possible to AI, in your own workflow and in the product. You have the judgment to know when it worked.
A deep-seated need to ship. We believe we win by outshipping everyone, and we hire engineers who treat blockers as things to bulldoze, not things to wait on.
Ownership by default. No one here is just on a team. Everyone owns and leads something, and you should want that.
TypeScript and Node.js experience (NestJS a plus). We care more about fundamentals than exact-stack trivia.
PostgreSQL knowledge and comfort with Docker.
An incredible attitude. You genuinely enjoy customer calls, you stay calm when production is on fire, and teammates describe you as the person they want in the room when things get hard.
Excellent communication, written and verbal. You can explain a webhook retry policy to a customer's IT admin and a data model tradeoff to our platform team with equal clarity.
Nice to have
Experience with enterprise procurement, finance, or ERP ecosystems (Ariba, Coupa, NetSuite, SAP, Workday).
Experience with iPaaS platforms or building connector frameworks.
What we offer
Top salary and equity
AI-paced culture
A team that plays like pros: high standards, high growth, no passengers
Ability to have strong customer context and autonomy
401K, Medical, Dental and Vision insurance

We are looking for a software development engineer to join the founding cohort of the Engineering and R\&D team within Leo Infrastructure and IP Security. The team defends the manufacturing lines, launch sites, and global ground infrastructure behind the constellation from the most sophisticated threat actors on the planet. You will build a neurosymbolic reasoning platform: large language model agents combined with a knowledge graph and real-time asset state store that ground every conclusion in verifiable fact, so every automated decision is auditable. The platform automates incident response, threat analysis, offensive security testing, and detection authoring, backed by a high-throughput streaming pipeline that takes a detection from concept to production in hours. The team is new and the surface area is wide: the features you ship become the system Leo's security teams run on from day one.

You will own building software features across the platform and deliver them end to end: clarify the requirements, write the design, ship the code, instrument the system, and keep it healthy in production. The features you own are concrete and high-consequence: the live state-of-the-world record that answers where every tracked device is, who last held it, and whether it is where it should be; consolidated detection that surfaces events from every Leo site type as one signal instead of siloed alarms; automated triage so security events arrive enriched and pre-adjudicated, with containment executed in seconds under human approval; self-service workflows that cut multi-day manual processes down to seconds; and the instrumentation that produces the metrics the security organization reports against. The next day you might pair with an applied scientist to backtest a candidate detection against retained telemetry before it ships, then pick up an operational ticket and automate away its root cause so no one handles it again. You will obsess over the two latencies that define the platform, the time from event to detection and the time from detection to containment action, and treat every manual step you find as a candidate for deletion. A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Roche.
Advances in AI, data, and computational sciences are transforming drug discovery and development. Roche’s Research and Early Development organisations at Genentech (gRED) and Pharma (pRED) have demonstrated how these technologies accelerate R&D, leveraging data and novel computational models to drive impact. Seamless data sharing and access to models across gRED and pRED are essential to maximising these opportunities. The new Computational Sciences Center of Excellence (CoE) is a strategic, unified group whose goal is to harness this transformative power of data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to assist our scientists in both pRED and gRED to deliver more innovative and transformative medicines for patients worldwide.
The Opportunity
At Roche’s AI for Drug Discovery (AI4DD) group (Prescient Design), we are building the machine learning platforms that enable researchers and engineers to move models from experimentation into reliable scientific and production workflows. We are seeking a Machine Learning Infrastructure Engineer to help build and operate the platforms that support model deployment, evaluation, promotion, monitoring, and lifecycle management across the organization. This role will contribute to our model-serving platform, and to the broader infrastructure required to make machine learning models easier to deploy, scale, observe, and safely incorporate into scientific and agentic workflows.
The scope extends beyond LLM serving. You will work with a range of machine learning and scientific models, including real-time and batch inference workloads, GPU-backed services, agentic applications, and our in-silico drug discovery workflows. This is a hands-on engineering role for someone who enjoys writing and shipping production software across application code, cloud infrastructure, Kubernetes, and distributed systems. Prior inference-platform experience is helpful but not required; prior experience in biotech or drug discovery is also helpful but not required; we value strong engineering fundamentals, curiosity, and the ability to take platform problems from design through production operation.
In this role, you will:
Design, implement, ship, and operate scalable model-serving infrastructure for machine learning, scientific, LLM, and agentic workloads.
Help evolve our internal model deployment platform into a reliable, self-service platform for teams across the organization.
Improve platform scalability and reliability, including scale-to-zero, faster model startup, workload isolation, traffic management, and reduction of request failures and latency bottlenecks.
Build observability and operational tooling for model usage, latency, reliability, resource consumption, inference cost, bottlenecks, and service-level indicators.
Improve the usability of model deployment by developing validated configuration interfaces, reusable deployment patterns, APIs, command-line tools, and documentation.
Help converge real-time and batch inference workflows onto shared platform capabilities where appropriate.

Microsoft is a company where passionate innovators come to collaborate, envision what can be, and take their careers further. This is a world of more possibilities, more innovation, more openness, and sky-is-the-limit thinking in a cloud-enabled world.
Within the Azure Monitor team, we are looking for a
Software Engineer II and Senior Software Engineer
to help build and evolve the Azure Monitor backend systems. This role is ideal for someone who can own complex, globally distributed systems end to end, drive architecture across teams, improve reliability and security at scale, and shape how AI-assisted and AI-agentic capabilities are safely applied to infrastructure operations. You will work on services that have to continue to scale for usage with the entire fleet, enabling telemetry scenarios for every workload.
Microsoft's Azure Data engineering team is leading the transformation of analytics in the world of data with products like databases, data integration, big data analytics, messaging and real-time analytics, and business intelligence. Our mission is to build the data platform for the age of AI, powering a new class of data-first applications, and driving a data culture.

Azure Monitor includes Log Analytics, Application Insights, Container Insights, Hosted Prometheus, Azure Managed Grafana, and more. Additionally, Azure Monitor is the platform upon which Microsoft Sentinel is built. We have a multi-billion dollar business that is growing rapidly, and we run some of the world’s highest scale observability services both for Microsoft internally and for our external customers, processing over 1.5 Exabytes of logs daily and tracking over 100 billion active metrics.
We embrace a fast-paced, startup-like culture focused on shipping early and often, with an emphasis on attention to detail, introspection, and accountability. Collaboration is at the heart of our team. We build on each other's ideas and empower engineers to innovate from the ground up, delivering world-class value at speed. If you're passionate about building the systems that power Azure's observability and health at hyperscale and thrive in an environment that values creativity, collaboration, and technical excellence, we'd love to hear from you.

Design, implement, test, deploy, and operate highly available distributed services and automation used to configure and migrate large-scale telemetry workloads that will be leveraged across the fleet.
Build and enhance APIs, tools, and subsystems for telemetry collection, routing, storage, and efficient data access.
Integrate advanced capabilities (e.g., machine learning–based anomaly detection and data validation) to enhance platform intelligence and insights.
Implement robust monitoring, alerting, and diagnostics and ensure production services run reliably, including participation in on-call rotations and incident response.
Collaborate with partner teams to deliver end-to-end observability solutions and contribute to design reviews and best practices that uphold high engineering standards.
Help evolve how the team builds with AI, championing agentic development practices and sharing repeatable patterns that improve engineering velocity and quality, as well as training and evolving AI to assist with non-coding scenarios such as site reliability engineering, support and administration.

Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 2+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C#, Java, .NET, or Python OR equivalent experience.

We are a Growth Invention company built to help the world’s most ambitious brands grow faster. Operating at the intersection of technology and marketing, we create what is next by pioneering ideas, acting fast, and moving further because standing still just is not in our DNA.

At DEPT®, you will find the freedom to explore, the space to collaborate, and the trust to make a real impact for our clients, for each other, and for the world we are helping to build.
What We Believe In
We build software for the world's most ambitious brands, and we're opinionated about how it gets made:
Code quality is a top priority. Style guides, code reviews, and best practices are how we move fast without breaking things. You'll also get your hands on a wide range of cutting-edge technology.
Great UI/UX is critical. Aesthetics, usability, and speed are all part of the product. A technically correct experience that feels bad isn't finished.
Collaboration wins projects. Great communication is the single strongest predictor of whether a project goes well.
We're pragmatic. We know what to build and what to leave alone, and we make real-world tradeoffs between cost, speed, and craft. Shipping something useful beats architecting something perfect.
We're intellectually curious. We're constantly learning through craft show & tells, lunch & learns, workshares, and active Slack channels full of talented engineers across the globe.

As a Senior Engineer, you own significant portions of a project and drive them to completion. You take a semi-defined problem, ask the questions that sharpen it, turn it into a plan, and ship it. You're past the stage of needing fully specified tasks handed to you, and you're building the judgment to know which task matters most.
You're comfortable working alongside product managers, engineers, marketing, sales, and finance, and you can explain your work to any of them without retreating into jargon. Most of what we build depends on getting those people to a shared understanding of what's being made and why.

Advocate for best practices in testing, security, performance, and CI/CD, and encourage others to do the same.
Work directly with working-level client stakeholders over email, on calls, and in person, and start building demo and presentation content of your own.
Apply AI and agentic capabilities to real client work, and contribute back to how the craft adopts them through reusable templates, prototyping sessions, and practical guidance for other teams.
Share what you learn, internally through Slack, brown bags, and DEPT U, and externally through articles or talks as project work allows.
What You Bring
Proven experience building and maintaining production-level backend systems used by real people.
Strong proficiency in Python.
Experience designing and integrating APIs and third-party systems.
Solid working knowledge of database platforms, both SQL and NoSQL.
Enough familiarity with modern frontend development (preferably Angular and Typescript) to read the code, review a PR, and debug across the stack.
Experience with at least one major cloud provider. Google Cloud preferred, AWS or Azure also welcome.
Daily, real-world use of GenAI productivity tools (Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Codex) in your development workflow.
A working understanding of core LLM concepts and where they're a good fit for a problem.
Fluency with version control (git), Agile processes, and CI/CD tooling.
The ability to research independently and know when to ask for help, without spinning wheels on already-solved problems.
A track record of "getting sh*t done" in a fast-paced environment.

Description
At Amazon, our SCOT Labs team owns and operates the experimentation platform that powers randomized controlled trials (RCTs) across Supply Chain Optimization Technologies (SCOT). We are the scientific gatekeepers for policy updates that govern how Amazon buys, stores, and moves billions of units of inventory worldwide. This is not traditional A/B testing: we are building the infrastructure and methodology to causally evaluate complex and interconnected supply chain interventions.
Our platform runs experiments that span millions of products and hundreds of fulfillment nodes simultaneously, measuring the real-world impact of policy changes on inventory health, customer experience, and operational cost. We are also advancing the science of causal inference in supply chain settings by developing novel approaches to treatment effect estimation, interference modeling, and emulation techniques that allow us to assess policy impact faster and more accurately than ever before.
The experiments you design and the methods you build here will directly determine which policies ship to production. These decisions influence hundreds of millions of dollars in weekly inventory investments, labor allocation for tens of thousands of associates, and Amazon's overall supply chain efficiency. Beyond operational impact, this team pushes the frontier of causal experimentation methodology and contributes to the broader scientific community with publications at top venues.
If you are a scientist who wants to shape how one of the world's largest supply chains makes decisions — solving causal inference challenges in real-world settings no academic lab or startup can replicate — this is the team for you.
Key job responsibilities
Partner with customer teams to design rigorous large-scale experiments (such as randomized controlled trials and quasi-experiments) to evaluate policy updates and model improvements across millions of products, hundreds of fulfillment nodes, and diverse business contexts
Build and maintain production-grade experimentation infrastructure and analytical tools using Python, SQL, Scala, and related technologies
Advance causal inference methodology for supply chain settings, including treatment effect estimation, interference modeling, and emulation techniques that accelerate policy evaluation. Ensure these methods are supported by both theoretical foundations and empirical evidence.
Translate complex research findings into clear insights and actionable recommendations for technical and non-technical stakeholders at all levels.
Contribute to Amazon's scientific community and the broader external research field through collaboration and publication in top-tier venues.
A day in the life
You might start the morning digging into results from a randomized trial running across millions of products, deciding whether the estimator you built last month is holding up and where it breaks. By the afternoon you could be designing the next experiment with a partner team where clean randomization is not available, because treated and control units draw on the same fulfillment network and inventory pools, and you need an approach that stays credible despite the spillover.
The role sits between developing methods and shipping them. You will build estimators and experiment designs for problems without textbook answers, prototype them in Python on real supply chain experiment data, and then put the ones that work into the platform other SCOT scientists use, writing Python, Scala, and SQL at a scale most scientists never encounter. You will also build supply chain emulation systems that replicate inventory dynamics end to end, so a design can be stress tested before it touches the real network.
The problems are open, the data is unmatched in scale, and the methods you build will shape how scientists across SCOT think about causal inference and move billions of dollars in inventory decisions. If you want to do measurement and experimentation research that actually ships, this is where you do it.
About The Team
The Forecasting and Labs Science team sits at the heart of Amazon's supply chain, building the science that determines what products are available, when, and at what cost for hundreds of millions of customers around the world. Our mission spans two deeply connected frontiers: pushing the boundaries of large-scale time series forecasting through foundation models that generalize across an enormous and diverse catalog of products, and building the experimentation and causal inference methodology that rigorously evaluates whether supply chain policy changes should ship to production.
We are a team of scientists who care deeply about both research rigor and real-world outcomes. We don't just publish: we ship. And we don't just ship: we measure, iterate, and raise the bar. On the forecasting side, we build foundation models at a scale unmatched in industry, running experiments across millions of products and exploring novel data generation techniques that open new frontiers in model generalization. On and off the robot sits an entire stack that makes the whole fleet run 24/7: on-robot drivers and services, streaming and telemetry, cloud backend, inference infrastructure, and the apps customers interact with every day. You'll build across all of it. One week it's a customer-facing feature in the app, the next it's the backend that serves it, the next it's the on-robot service that feeds it data.

https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/44814.description_preview:
About Yuzu
Health insurance is a $1.3 trillion industry powered by fax machines, Excel macros, and misaligned incentives. Yuzu is rebuilding health plan administration from scratch. We're replacing the patchwork of disconnected vendors, hidden fees, and opaque pricing with a single platform that gives employers real transparency and control over their health spend.
We bring innovative health plans to life by administering plans that expand healthcare access for small employers, deliver price transparency to members and providers, and simplify eligibility for brokers. Yuzu’s goal is to make it as easy for any business to create and manage a custom health plan as it is to create a storefront on Shopify.
We’re backed by General Catalyst, Anthropic, Chemistry, Lachy Groom and many unicorn founders, including leaders at Stripe, OpenAI, Brex, Deel, Mercury, and Notion.
Our team is small, technical, and moves fast. We care about craftsmanship, think from first principles, and believe insurance is one of the most important but under-built categories in software.
The Role
Product engineers own features end-to-end, not just the code. You'll work directly with customers and our operations team to identify product gaps, find the clearest path through ambiguous problems, and ship new features from 0 to 1. There is no PM in the middle. You own outcomes, not just code.
You will move across the stack to deliver features, touching frontend, backend, databases, APIs, and more.
Gergely Orosz of
The Pragmatic Engineer
aptly describes what we look for in “product-minded engineers”:
"Product-minded engineers are developers with lots of interest in the product itself. They want to understand why decisions are made, how people use the product, and love to be involved in making product decisions. They're someone who would likely make a good product manager if they ever decide to give up the joy of engineering."
Location and Culture
We're strong believers in an in-person culture. Our HQ is in NYC near Union Square.
Yuzu exists because healthcare infrastructure is broken. Not because the problems are inherently hard, but because bad incentives have made simple processes complicated. We're building the platform that allows health plan innovators to skip the mess and move fast. That mission shapes how we operate day to day.
We don't soften bad news, hedge our conclusions, or let politeness outrun clarity. If something is broken, we say so. To each other, to our customers, and in our product decisions. We expect you to do the same.
We're a small team where everyone operates full-stack on problems. You'll sometimes do work that isn't in your job title, and that should sound like a perk, not a burden. We ship, learn, and iterate. Healthcare is full of "that's just how it works" explanations. We question that default. We want someone who reasons through tradeoffs independently rather than waiting for a playbook.
Yuzu isn't the right place for everyone, and we'd rather be upfront about that. We have very few meetings, flexible outlines, and a lot of autonomy. No one’s checking whether you look busy. You'll need to develop your own sense of what matters and act on it. Some people find that energizing. Others find it disorienting. Whether Yuzu is the right fit is just a question of which environment makes you do your best work.
What We're Looking For
Complexity wrangler
We move money, operate in a complex space, and serve employers, members, brokers, and a multitude of other user types. Our systems are complex by nature. You're someone who can navigate that complexity and keep things simple where it counts.
Thrives in chaos
Things change, surprises happen, and not everything is in our control. You're comfortable with ambiguity and don't let it slow you down.
Sweats the details
We’re building a platform that plays a major role in all of our members’ lives. Every pixel, every error state, every edge case matters. You care about the user experience as much as the architecture underneath it.
AI-excited
Most of our code is written by AI. We're figuring out what software engineering looks like when that's true, and we want people who are energized by that, not threatened by it.
Requirements
Smart > Experienced
We don't care what languages or frameworks you've used before. If you're smart, you'll figure it out. We use Typescript, Svelte, and Nest, but what matters to us is that you can build things that work.
AI-native
You are on the cutting edge of AI tools. You use Cursor, Codex, Claude, or your favorite CLI. Not as a novelty, but as a core part of how you generate code and think through problems.
Full-stack
You can build and ship a feature end-to-end. Frontend, backend, database, deploy. No hand-offs, no waiting around.
Example Projects
YuzuSign
D*cuSign was a friction point, so a single engineer replaced it in weeks with a purpose-built signing platform deeply integrated into the rest of our stack. What required thousands of engineers within a publicly traded company is now within reach of a single focused engineer with the right tools.
Real-Time Money Ledger
We move hundreds of millions of dollars every month. Most platforms piece together where that money is with batch reports and spreadsheets. We built a real-time double-entry ledger that tracks every financial event as it happens.
Cash Cards
When members pay out of pocket for care, the experience is usually clunky: pay upfront, submit receipts, wait for reimbursement. We built a prepaid health card that simplifies that experience for members and grants them greater access to affordable care. And because we own the full stack, every swipe flows straight through to the same ledger and claims system that manages their benefits.
Benefits
$160k – $265k plus equity depending on experience
Unlimited vacation days
Medical, dental, & vision insurance
401K with 1% match
Unlimited AI tokens & tool budget — Cursor, Claude, Codex, you name it
Apple equipment
Free lunch daily and plent

Radical AI is replacing an R&D process that currently takes 10+ years and $100 million to produce a single discovery. Our self-driving lab platform combines AI with autonomous robotics to run experiments, analyze results, and iterate—continuously, without human bottlenecks. For industries like aerospace, automotive, defense, energy, manufacturing, semiconductors, and space, that means breakthroughs in weeks instead of years.
The Role
We're looking for a generalist Machine Learning Engineer to turn ML research into capabilities that hold up in production, inside the platform that runs our autonomous lab. A model that can't be trained reliably, served efficiently, and trusted by the scientists using it doesn't count. Your job is to make sure it does.
You'll work side by side with our ML Researchers: designing experiments together, building training pipelines, evaluating models, and taking what works into production. You'll own the engineering that makes that possible, from data preparation and reproducible training to inference performance, product integration, and monitoring after release. Nobody hands you a spec; you'll help decide what's worth building, then build it.
This is a hands-on role across the full ML lifecycle. One week you're in the weeds with a researcher, debugging a training run or implementing a new approach. The next you're standing up a serving endpoint, running down a production failure, or rebuilding the pipeline that gets the next model into users' hands.
This is not a research role, and it's not a pure infrastructure role. We need strong software engineering fundamentals, real experience training and deploying models, and the judgment to trade model quality against reliability, latency, and cost, and to defend those calls when researchers push back. If your instinct is to hand off a model rather than own how it performs, or to wait for clear requirements before moving, this isn't the right fit. Success is simple: research improvements become measurable improvements in Radical's product.
What You'll Work On
Partner with ML Researchers. Turn research ideas into working implementations, co-design experiments, and surface engineering constraints before they become blockers.
Build and run training pipelines. Own the workflows for training and fine-tuning models: datasets, configurations, failure triage, and compute efficiency.
Make experiments reproducible. Track code, data, environments, and model artifacts so any result can be reproduced and built on with confidence.
Evaluate models for product use. Build the datasets and tests that measure model quality, expose failure modes, and decide, with evidence, whether a candidate is ready to ship.
Deploy and integrate models. Turn research code into tested, maintainable components and services, and work with product and platform engineers to put them into real scientific workflows.
Improve inference performance. Profile and optimize latency, throughput, memory, and cost without giving up the quality the product depends on.
Own performance after launch. Monitor model and service behavior, run down regressions, keep releases and rollbacks safe, and feed what you learn into the next round of research.
Improve how the team ships ML. Build the shared tooling and automation that shrink the path from a promising experiment to a dependable product capability.
What We're Looking For
You've taken ML models from experimentation and training all the way into production, and owned the systems that kept them running.
4+ years in ML engineering, research engineering, or a closely related software engineering role.
Strong Python and real software engineering discipline: testing, code review, packaging, and system design that someone else can maintain.
Deep hands-on experience with PyTorch or a comparable framework. You've implemented, trained, evaluated, and debugged models yourself, not just called them.
A working command of dataset quality, train/validation splits, overfitting, data leakage, and why offline metrics so often lie about production performance.
Experience building data pipelines on cloud infrastructure, with containers and GPU workloads.
Experience deploying models through services or batch pipelines, with real attention to observability, reliability, and operating cost.
You engage with researchers as a peer, not through a translator. You pick up unfamiliar approaches quickly and make sound implementation calls while the requirements are still moving.
A generalist's range and an owner's instinct. You move between model code, data, infrastructure, and product integration, and you don't stop until the whole system works.
Able to work on-site at the Brooklyn Navy Yard.
Nice to Have
Experience with LLM training or fine-tuning, model serving, or agent systems.
Distributed training, GPU profiling, or inference optimization experience.
Familiarity with experiment tracking, dataset and model versioning, and automated model release workflows.
Experience with scientific ML, optimization, reinforcement learning, or sequential decision-making.
A background in scientific computing, materials, chemistry, robotics, or lab automation.
Experience shipping ML on a small team where the roadmap changes as fast as the science.
What Success Looks Like
In your first six to twelve months:
Models built with our researchers are live in Radical's product and delivering measurable improvements.
Training and evaluation workflows are reproducible and reliable, and the rest of the team actually uses them.
Every model release has clear quality criteria, automated checks, production monitoring, and a rollback path that works.
The path from promising experiment to production release is measurably faster and far less manual.
Production failures and user feedback flow directly into new datasets, evaluations, and research priorities.
Model quality, inference performance, and operating cost are understood, tracked, and improved together, not traded off by accident

Most businesses have a camera on the wall, and almost none of them use what it sees. Our client, a venture-backed applied AI startup, turns ordinary store cameras into live operational data for restaurant, retail and convenience brands.
Their platform already runs in thousands of locations, and new enterprise contracts are about to multiply that footprint many times over. They need a senior engineer to make computer vision work reliably at that scale.

Camera and install standards so large rollouts go smoothly the first time

Python for inference, evaluation and training workflows
Elixir and OTP for the core platform: concurrency, fault tolerance and real-time pipelines

An AI-first engineering team that uses coding agents and modern AI tools every day

4+ years as a software engineer, including real time at a venture-backed startup

Strong Python
Elixir or another functional language is a big plus, not a must
Open-source work or side projects are a big plus
THIS PROBABLY ISN'T FOR YOU IF
Your background is pure ML research or LLM-only, or you mainly train models from scratch

You're a manager or executive no longer coding every day
You've never shipped computer vision or ML to production
PACKAGE AND LOCATION
$185K to $205K base plus meaningful equity
Top-tier health benefits and flexible PTO
Fully remote in the United States, with at least 5 hours overlap with Mountain Time and one team on-site visit a quarter
WORK AUTHORIZATION (IMPORTANT)
You must be a US citizen or US Green Card holder.
Visa sponsorship is not available now or in the future, and we cannot consider H-1B, OPT, TN or any other visa holders.

https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/44806.description_preview:
DESCRIPTION: BeaconFire is based in Central NJ, specializing in Software Development, Web
Development, and Business Intelligence; looking for candidates who are good communicators and
self-motivated. You will play a key role in building, maintaining, and operating integrations,
reporting pipelines, and data transformation systems.
Qualifications:
● Passion for data and a deep desire to learn.
● Master’s Degree in Computer Science/Information Technology, Data Analytics/Data
Science, or related discipline.
● Intermediate Python. Experience in data processing is a plus. (Numpy, Pandas, etc)
● Experience with relational databases (SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL, etc.)
● Strong written and verbal communication skills.
● Ability to work both independently and as part of a team.
Responsibilities:
● Collaborate with the analytics team to find reliable data solutions to meet the business
needs.
● Design and implement scalable ETL or ELT processes to support the business demand for
data.
● Perform data extraction, manipulation, and production from database tables.
● Build utilities, user-defined functions, and frameworks to better enable data flow patterns.
● Build and incorporate automated unit tests, participate in integration testing efforts.
● Work with teams to resolve operational & performance issues.
● Work with architecture/engineering leads and other teams to ensure quality solutions are
implemented, and engineering best practices are defined and adhered to.

Description
Amazon Robotics is looking for an experienced Systems Development Engineer to join the Imperium Data Services team in Austin. Data Services owns the source-of-truth data behind network automation across Amazon's fulfillment network: what devices exist, where they live, how they should be configured, which credentials they use, and what state they are actually in. Our services handle nearly a billion API calls a month and sit underneath config generation, deployment, and lifecycle workflows for hundreds of thousands of IP-enabled devices across thousands of sites. When our data is wrong, networks break; when it is right and fast, the rest of automation can run with confidence.
In this role you will partner with software, systems, and network engineers around the world to build and operate the data layer that network automation depends on. You will work on high-throughput APIs and data stores, collection of live device state, data pipelines, and the validation and staging gates that stop bad data before it reaches production devices. Network engineers and automation teams rely on the accuracy of what we serve. Your work will let them get answers in seconds and spend their time on hard problems instead of manual data cleanup. We value correctness, simplicity, and operational excellence in our designs.
Key job responsibilities
As a Systems Development Engineer on Data Services, you will design, build, and operate highly available services that model network devices, sites, and credentials, serving thousands of requests per second to automation workflows across the fulfillment network. You will build systems that collect the observed state of devices, including hardware inventory, firmware, interfaces, and neighbors, compare it against intended state, and surface drift before it causes customer impact. You will own data quality end to end, from schema design and validation at write time to staged, reviewable data changes, data health monitoring, and alarms that catch bad data before it reaches device configurations. You will lead migrations of legacy data sources onto modern APIs without disrupting the dozens of downstream teams that depend on them. You will take part in on-call, drive root-cause analysis and corrective actions, and turn recurring operational pain into automation, using AWS (CDK, Lambda, DynamoDB, S3, OpenSearch) and CI/CD pipelines to automate infrastructure and deployments.
Ideal candidates enjoy working where distributed systems meet network data. You communicate clearly, turn ambiguous requirements into simple, durable designs, and care as much about how a service runs in production as how it is built. You will work in a fast-moving, collaborative environment with partner teams who depend on your systems every day.
A day in the life
You will be a part of an agile development team following innovative best practices in software development where you will work on technical designs, architecture and coding. To build our applications, you will interact with network engineering teams to gather requirements, provide technical solutions and develop the software that are required in defining our next generation products.

401(k) Plan

Our team exists so that network engineers and automation teams can trust the data that runs Amazon's fulfillment network. We own the systems of record for network devices, sites, and credentials, plus the systems that observe what is actually running on devices in the field. Config generation, deployments, and lifecycle workflows across Imperium are all built on these services. We are accountable for making that data correct, fast, and safe to change, and we start from the customer: every bad record we prevent is an outage a network engineer never has to debug. As part of Data Services, you will work with automation, network engineering, and build teams across Amazon, and you will own your systems end to end, from design through operating them in production for hundreds of thousands of devices.

GNC Engineer - Develop Controls for Spacecraft That Assemble Themselves in Orbit
Golden, CO | On-site
Opportunity Summary
A venture-backed space startup is building modular spacecraft that dock and latch together in orbit using electromagnetic actuation, creating vehicles far larger than anything that fits inside a rocket fairing. Controlling a spacecraft whose mass, inertia, and shape change as it assembles is an open problem, and this team is solving it with flight hardware.
We are adding a talented early-career GNC engineer to a strong, senior controls team. You will work across attitude control, estimation, and nonlinear control of electromagnetic actuators, taking algorithms from simulation into flight software and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The bar is high, and in return you will get real ownership and direct mentorship from engineers who have flown GNC systems.
About Us
We are a venture-backed space technology startup in Golden, Colorado building modular spacecraft that launch as compact units and join together in orbit to form larger, more capable vehicles. The core technology has already flown in multiple on-orbit and microgravity demonstrations, and a newly outfitted facility is supporting the move toward larger hardware and a free-flying demonstration. The team is small and senior, with engineers who have shipped hardware at leading launch, satellite, and defense companies, and every engineer owns a real piece of the vehicle.
Job Duties
Develop attitude determination and control algorithms in C++ and Python for de-tumble, pointing, slewing, and momentum management
Model and control spacecraft whose inertia and structure change as modules join and separate
Design and tune nonlinear controllers for electromagnetic actuators used in docking and relative motion
Build simulations and run 6DOF Monte Carlo analyses to verify performance
Take algorithms into flight software and validate them through hardware-in-the-loop testing
Support sensor and actuator trade studies and help define GNC requirements
Support flight operations and on-orbit anomaly investigations
Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in aerospace, mechanical, or electrical engineering, physics, mathematics, or a related field
2+ years of professional or graduate research experience in controls, GNC, or dynamics
Strong grounding in control theory, including nonlinear control
Software development experience in C++ and Python
Track record that shows you are performing well ahead of your years of experience
Comfortable as a generalist who can pick up new areas quickly
U.S. person status (U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, refugee, or asylee) required under ITAR
Preferred Experience
Experience with electromagnets, electromagnetic actuators, or magnetic force and torque modeling
Graduate research (MS or PhD) in controls, electromagnetics, or related areas
Spacecraft ADCS experience, including attitude dynamics, quaternion kinematics, and state estimation such as MEKF
Experience with flexible-body or multi-body dynamics
Hardware-in-the-loop testing or real-world deployment of control algorithms
Experience with Git and collaborative software workflows
Why Join Us
Work on a GNC problem that has no textbook answer: controlling spacecraft that reconfigure in orbit
Learn directly from senior GNC engineers while owning meaningful parts of the system
Take your algorithms from simulation to flight hardware
Early-employee stock options with meaningful upside as the platform moves toward operational missions
Fast growth on a small team, where engineers who deliver take on broader ownership quickly
Medical, dental, and vision coverage
Short- and long-term disability insurance and life insurance
Paid parental leave
Three weeks of paid vacation and 10 or more paid holidays annually
Compensation Details
$100,000 - $140,000 + equity
