We build the diagnostic tests that every accelerator server runs before it becomes sellable, and we decide which failures block a host, which route to a technician for repair, and which are noise.
That gate only works if we can see through it. We are hiring a Software Development Engineer II to build the data and analytics systems that tell us what our tests are actually doing across the fleet. You will build the pipelines that ingest diagnostic results from tens of thousands of servers, the dashboards that make test behavior legible, and the metrics and alarms that tell us a test has started failing on a hardware generation before it costs us a week of capacity. When the team decides whether a diagnostic has enough evidence to move from observation into blocking production, your data answers that question.
This is a software engineering role, not a reporting role. You will write and operate production code, own the alarms and metrics that page us, and build detection for trends nobody is watching yet. You will work directly with hardware, firmware, provisioning, and data center operations teams who act on what you build.
You are fluent in Python and SQL and have built production data pipelines at scale. Experience with Amazon Redshift, Apache Spark, workflow orchestration, and dashboarding in Grafana or QuickSight maps directly to what you will work on here. Experience with telemetry or diagnostic data from a large server fleet, or with defining metrics and anomaly detection on operational time-series data, will have you productive faster. Familiarity with server hardware or data center operations is a plus, not a requirement — we will teach you the hardware.
Key job responsibilities
Design, build, and operate production data pipelines that ingest diagnostic, telemetry, and repair-ticket data from the Trainium and Inferentia fleet into a warehouse other teams query with confidence.
Build and own the metrics, alarms, and anomaly detection that surface test regressions, failure-rate shifts, and new failure signatures across hardware generations without a human going looking for them.
Build dashboards and visualizations that make fleet and test health legible to engineers, hardware partners, and leadership, covering failure rates, failure-signature breakdowns, first pass yield, and repair latency.
Analyze large-scale fleet data to find root cause behind failure trends, and separate genuine hardware faults from software defects and test noise — a distinction that decides whether a failure reaches a technician or an engineer.
Define the evidence standard that gates operational decisions, including whether a diagnostic has soaked long enough and cleanly enough in the fleet to move from observation mode into blocking production.
Improve data quality and pipeline reliability so downstream consumers trust the numbers without re-deriving them.
Write clear analyses and design documents for technical and non-technical readers, including leadership.
A day in the life
You start by checking an alarm that fired overnight: a diagnostic's failure rate climbed on one server generation. You query the failure signatures, find the increase concentrates in one component and one data center, and hand the breakdown to the hardware team by mid-morning. The rest of the day goes to a pipeline you are building to join repair outcomes against diagnostic results, so the team can measure how often a repair actually fixes the fault it was dispatched for. You close the day reviewing a teammate's code review and answering an operations partner who needs a new cut of yield data.
About The Team
MLA Vetting sits between hardware manufacturing and customer-ready capacity. We own the diagnostic test suites and the triage framework that turn a raw hardware failure into a specific, actionable repair, and we own the fleet-scale evidence that drives hardware and firmware improvements upstream. Our work is measured in how fast a server reaches sellable and how often it gets there on the first try.

Mid-Level Computer Engineer
Description:
Computer hardware and software engineers’ research, design, develop, and test computer hardware and software programs. Hardware refers to computer chips, circuit boards, computer systems, and related equipment such as keyboards, modems, and printers.
Computer software engineers develop software systems that control computers.
Computer hardware engineers work exclusively with computers and computer-related equipment.
In addition to design and development duties, computer hardware engineers supervise the manufacturing and installation of computers and computer-related equipment.
Computer software engineers develop new computer software systems and incorporate new technologies into a rapidly growing range of applications.
Computer software engineers apply the principles and techniques of computer science, engineering, and mathematical analysis to the design, development, testing, and evaluation of the software and systems that enable computers to perform their many applications.
Software engineers analyze users’ needs and design, construct, test, and maintain computer applications software or systems.
Computer software engineers can be involved in the design and development of many types of software, including software for operating systems and network distribution, and compilers, which convert programs for execution on a computer.
They also solve technical problems that arise.
Software engineers must possess strong programming skills but are more concerned with developing algorithms and analyzing and solving programming problems than with actually writing code.
The programming languages most often used are C, C++, and Java, with Fortran and COBOL used less commonly.
Requirements
Experience:
3 years of professional experience in computer design, software development or computer networks
Education:
Bachelor's level degree in Computer, Electrical or Electronics Engineering or Mathematics with field of concentration in computer science.
Security Clearance:
Security clearance required SECRET level.
Location:
Norfolk, VA

Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Engineer
Location: Oklahoma City, OK
Reports to: VP, Data Science
Employment Type: Salary, Exempt Full-Time
About Us
Western Natural Resources (WNR) is a privately held, Oklahoma City–based oil and gas company focused on acquiring, developing, and operating high-quality upstream energy assets. Founded through a strategic partnership between Centalion and experienced energy leaders, WNR combines deep industry expertise, disciplined execution, and a long-term approach to building a premier energy company.
WNR is a rapidly growing organization with an entrepreneurial culture where collaboration, integrity, safety, and accountability are central to how we operate. As the company expands its asset base and team, employees have the opportunity to make a meaningful impact, work closely with experienced industry leaders, and help build the infrastructure and culture of a growing energy company.
Position Summary
Western Natural Resources is hiring an AI/ML Engineer to build the machine learning models and analytics applications that help the company make better technical and commercial decisions — turning the data on our Databricks lakehouse into tools that engineers, operations, accounting, land, and leadership use every day.
This is a hands-on role on a small team. You will work side by side with employees across the organization to understand the problems they are trying to solve, build and validate the models behind the answers in Databricks, and ship them as applications people actually use. We build with agentic AI coding tools as a normal part of the workflow and expect the same here — used with judgment, with results verified against the data.
Key Responsibilities
Work directly with engineers and business stakeholders across reservoir engineering, operations, accounting, and land to understand the problems they face and turn them into well-scoped analytics solutions.
Build, train, validate, and deploy machine learning models in Databricks - forecasting, predictive, and optimization models that support operating and capital decisions, using MLflow to track experiments and manage model versions.
Build applications and dashboards that put model outputs in front of users across the company - tools people use to make decisions, not one-off analyses.
Develop with agentic AI coding tools (Claude Code or similar) to prototype and ship quickly, verifying results against the data and against the judgment of the people who will use them.
Validate models rigorously: backtest, quantify uncertainty, and explain in plain terms where a model can and cannot be trusted.
Deploy and monitor models and applications in production - including retraining and catching drift or degraded results before a user does.
Partner with the data engineering team to build on the lakehouse's curated tables, and bring data needs back to the platform.
Work alongside users through iteration: gather feedback, refine the tools, and document and train so adoption sticks.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Statistics, Data Science, or a related field.
Upstream oil and gas experience in working knowledge of the problems engineers and business stakeholders solve, such as production and reserves forecasting, well performance, and economics
+ years building and deploying machine learning models, from data preparation and feature engineering through training, validation, and deployment
Strong hands-on Python and SQL. This role writes code daily.
Solid foundation in statistics and machine learning: model selection, validation, and diagnosing when a model is wrong
Experience building applications, dashboards, or APIs that put model results in front of end users
Working fluency with agentic AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, or similar), and the judgment to know when their output has to be verified
Git-based version control and code review as a normal part of your workflow
Ability to work directly with non-technical stakeholders, translate business problems into analytical solutions, and communicate clearly in writing and in person
Ability to work independently in a small-team environment
Preferred Qualifications
Master's degree in Data Science, Analytics, or a related technical field
Databricks experience, including MLflow, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, and job orchestration, and production experience with Spark (PySpark and Spark SQL)
Building LLM-powered or agentic applications in production
BI tools such as Spotfire or Power BI
What We Offer
Competitive base salary + performance-based incentives
Direct influence on how WNR makes decisions, with tools you build used across the company
A modern cloud data and AI stack, with real input into the tools and architecture
Flat, collaborative team structure with fast decision-making
Physical Requirements
Ability to perform the essential functions of the position, including sitting, standing, walking, communicating, and using standard office or job-related equipment. May require lifting, travel, working outdoors, or use of personal protective equipment.

Familiarity with 6D pose estimation, point cloud processing, or visual-servoing.

Who We Are
Nuro believes self-driving vehicles are the most immediate and profound opportunity for AI to drive positive change in the physical world. Safer streets, more time for what matters, and easier access to the world around us, that’s why we’re building a universal autonomy platform: self-driving for all roads and all rides.
Founded in 2016, Nuro is a physical AI company developing Level 4 autonomous driving technology for a wide range of vehicles, use cases, and markets. Powered by the Nuro Driver™, our universal autonomy platform enables the global mobility ecosystem to deploy autonomy at scale, from robotaxis and logistics fleets to personal vehicles.
With years of real-world deployment experience and a flexible, partner-led business model, Nuro is working toward a future where millions of autonomous vehicles powered by our technology help make everyday life safer, easier, and more connected.
Nuro has raised over $2B in capital from Uber, NVIDIA, Google, Softbank, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, and other leading investors.
About The Role
Nuro operates real self-driving vehicles on public roads today — not a research platform, not ADAS. The Embedded Software Engineering team builds the software for the safety-critical embedded controllers that connect the Nuro Driver™ to the vehicle: the devices that command steering, braking, and propulsion, alongside other vehicle actuators, distribute and monitor power, monitor vehicle motion, and bring the vehicle to a safe state when something goes wrong.
As an Embedded Software Engineer, you will work across the full stack of multicore automotive microcontrollers from RTOS, drivers, and scheduler up through middleware and application components that talk to the vehicle, and help extend that stack as our hardware evolves. You will bring the Nuro Driver™ up on new vehicle platforms alongside OEM and supplier engineers, and see your code drive real vehicles on public roads. ABOUT NIRVA
Nirva is building the first AI fashion accessory for your mind — a necklace or bracelet that privately listens only to the wearer to enable proactive journaling, emotion tracking, and life coaching. Think Oura Ring for your Mind.
Backed by Lightspeed and South Park Commons, recognized at CES within 90 days of founding, and launching in the U.S. this fall. Co-founders bring backgrounds from Meta Reality Labs (Quest, Ray-Ban glasses) and fashion industry.
THE ROLE
We’re looking for an AI Audio / Voice Engineer to build the audio front door to Nirva’s intelligence layer: the systems that capture only the wearer, reliably, privately, and with as much processing on device as possible. This is the trust foundation for the whole product. If Nirva cannot tell who is speaking, reject everyone else, and do it in noisy real life without draining the battery or sending raw audio where it should not go, nothing built on top of it works. You will own voiceprint, on-device audio, and the technical systems behind our privacy promise, and work directly with the founding team to build them from the ground up.
WHAT YOU'LL OWN
Voiceprint: build speaker enrollment, voice embeddings, verification and identification so Nirva recognizes the wearer and separates them from bystanders, family, coworkers, and media
Tune and evaluate voiceprint in the real world: false accepts, false rejects, noisy cafes, walking, wind, cars, quiet rooms, illness, and voice drift over time, plus re-enrollment and recovery flows
Anti-spoofing and trust protections: replay and impersonation resistance, liveness signals where relevant, and clear fallbacks when confidence is low
On-device audio: design the on-device pipeline for voice activity detection, segmentation, speaker filtering, audio preprocessing, noise suppression, and streaming to speech recognition, with tight latency, power, thermal, and memory budgets
Decide the on-device vs. cloud split for each audio task and build graceful fallbacks when connectivity, battery, or confidence changes
Trust by design: on-device first processing, bystander exclusion, consent and recording controls, encryption in transit and at rest, data minimization, retention and deletion controls, and user-visible controls that match what the system actually does
Build evals and data pipelines for audio: test sets across people, accents, environments, and devices, failure analysis, and systematic debugging of real user-facing failures
Partner with product, design, and the memory / AI teams so clean, trusted, wearer-only audio becomes transcripts, memories, and experiences users can rely on

2+ years of full-time engineering experience, or a PhD in computer science, electrical engineering, machine learning, speech / audio, or a related field, plus 2 applied internships (industry or applied research) where you shipped or evaluated real systems
Deep, hands-on knowledge of at least one of these, and working knowledge of the other two: 1) voiceprint / speaker verification and identification, 2) on-device audio ML, 3) trust, privacy, and security for audio sensing
Hands-on experience with speech and audio ML in production: speaker embeddings, diarization, VAD, streaming audio, speech-to-text interfaces, audio preprocessing, or speech event detection
Experience running ML on device or at the edge: model quantization, distillation, latency and power optimization, and working within hardware constraints
Strong eval mindset for audio: you can build a test set, measure false accept / false reject and word error tradeoffs, find why a failure happened, and improve the system, not just the demo
Strong product engineering instincts and high ownership: you identify what needs to happen and drive it to shipped quality
Comfortable with ambiguous, human-centered problems where “good” is not easy to measure, and energized by 0-to-1 work, fast iteration, and early-stage startup intensity
Based in San Francisco and able to work in person
Strong signals (nice-to-haves)
Shipped always-on or low-power audio, wearables, hearables, or mobile audio products
Experience with anti-spoofing, voice liveness, or biometric security and its failure modes
iOS audio, Core ML, or embedded / DSP experience
Privacy engineering, on-device personal data systems, or consumer trust and safety for sensing products
